_comment: A snapshot of `otelq savings reduction --since 7d` and `otelq savings bytes --since 7d`, taken on this machine on the date below. It exists because CLAUDE.md.tmpl quotes those figures in prose and nothing tied the prose to the tool that produced it, so the numbers dated the paragraph and drifted (#578): the literals it carried until this snapshot -- 97.4 MB read, 26.9 KB printed, 223 calls, 3,616:1, against 41.7 MB of tool output -- had moved by more than an order of magnitude in the ratio. tests/otel-savings-rollup.test.js formats these fields and asserts each one appears in the paragraph, so a hand-edited literal goes red. To refresh the claim, re-run both commands, replace this file, and rewrite the prose from it in the same commit. Both windows are rolling 7-day windows over one machine's own data, so a rerun never reproduces a snapshot exactly -- the test compares the prose against THIS file, never against a fresh query. `truncated` is the rollup's own warning that jsonq rotated its counter part-way through the window; it was false when this was taken, so the window is whole. The reduction report reads ~/.local/share/claude-metrics/filters.jsonl and needs no backend; the bytes report is a LogQL query, so it needs Loki reachable. bytes_by_tool is dropped from the bytes report here: the paragraph quotes only the total.
